   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}
   384	
   385	CL functions used in the paper are frequently defined over a ``large'' field
   386	$\F_{2^t}$ (e.g., the CL functions used in the low degree tests of
   387	Section~\ref{sec:ldt}).
   388	However, the introspection protocol in Section~\ref{sec:introspection} handles
   389	CL functions defined over $\F_2$.
   390	The following definition and lemma show that CL functions over prime power
   391	fields can be viewed as CL functions over the prime field via a ``downsizing''
   392	operation.
   393	
   394	\begin{definition}[Downsizing CL functions]
   395	  \label{def:cl-downsize}
   396	  Let $V = \F_{q}^n$ be a linear space for a prime power $q=p^t$ for odd $t$.
   397	  Let $L: V \to V$ be a function.
   398	  Let $\downsize(\cdot)$ denote the downsize map from
   399	  Section~\ref{sec:finite-fields} corresponding to the basis
   400	  $\{e_1,\ldots,e_t\}$ of $\F_q$ over $\F_p$ specified by
   401	  Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_basis}.
   402	  In particular, $\downsize$ is linear over $\F_p$, and by
   403	  Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_subspace}, the set $\downsize(V)$ is the linear space
   404	  $\F_p^{nt}$.
   405	  Define the \emph{downsized function} $L^\downsize : \downsize(V) \to
   406	  \downsize(V)$ by $L^\downsize = \downsize \circ L \circ \downsize^{-1}$.
   407	\end{definition}

    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]

    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :

    61	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.

    80	  | _, .zero, _ => True

   758	tuples of vectors on the partition registers. -/
   759	private noncomputable def coordinatePartitionEquiv {K ι J : Type*}
   760	    [AddCommMonoid K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   761	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   762	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) : (ι → K) ≃ ∀ j, V j → K where
   763	  toFun x := fun _ a => x a
   764	  invFun x := ∑ j, extendRegister (V j) (x j)
   765	  left_inv x := by
   766	    funext a
   767	    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   768	    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (fun b => x b)) a = x a
   769	    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   770	    · simp [extendRegister, haj]
   771	    · intro i _ hij
   772	      have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   773	        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   774	      simp [extendRegister, hai]
   775	    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   776	  right_inv x := by
   777	    funext j a
   778	    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (x i)) a.1 = x j a
   779	    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   780	    · simp [extendRegister, a.2]
   781	    · intro i _ hij
   782	      have hai : a.1 ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   783	        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai a.2
   784	      simp [extendRegister, hai]
   785	    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   786	
   787	private theorem coordinatePartitionEquiv_apply {K ι J : Type*}
   788	    [AddCommMonoid K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   789	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   790	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) (j : J) (a : V j) :
   791	    coordinatePartitionEquiv V hDisjoint hCover x j a = x a := rfl
   792	
   793	private theorem extendRegister_partition_apply {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   794	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   795	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   796	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) (j : J) :
   797	    extendRegister (V j) (coordinatePartitionEquiv V hDisjoint hCover x j) =
   798	      coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   799	  ext a
   800	  by_cases ha : a ∈ V j
   801	  · simp [extendRegister, coordinateRestriction, ha, coordinatePartitionEquiv_apply]
   802	  · simp [extendRegister, coordinateRestriction, ha]

   804	/-- Reindex the cardinality of a filtered finite type along an equivalence. -/
   805	private theorem card_filter_equiv {A B : Type*} [Fintype A]
   806	    [Fintype B] (e : A ≃ B) (p : A → Prop) (q : B → Prop)
   807	    [DecidablePred p] [DecidablePred q] (hpq : ∀ a, p a ↔ q (e a)) :
   808	    (Finset.univ.filter p).card = (Finset.univ.filter q).card := by
   809	  classical
   810	  have hmap : (Finset.univ.filter p).map e.toEmbedding = Finset.univ.filter q := by
   811	    ext b
   812	    simp only [Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   813	    constructor
   814	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
   815	      exact (hpq a).mp ha
   816	    · intro hb
   817	      exact ⟨e.symm b, (hpq (e.symm b)).mpr (by simpa using hb), by simp⟩
   818	  rw [← hmap, Finset.card_map]
   819	
   820	private theorem card_filter_pi_apply_mem {J : Type*} [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   821	    (B : J → Type*) [∀ j, Fintype (B j)] [∀ j, DecidableEq (B j)]
   822	    (j : J) (s : Finset (B j)) :
   823	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (∀ i, B i)).filter fun x => x j ∈ s).card =
   824	      s.card * ∏ i : {i // i ≠ j}, Fintype.card (B i.1) := by
   825	  let u : ∀ i, Finset (B i) := fun _ => Finset.univ
   826	  have hs : s ⊆ u j := Finset.subset_univ s
   827	  rw [← Fintype.piFinset_univ]
   828	  rw [← Fintype.piFinset_update_eq_filter_piFinset_mem u j hs]
   829	  rw [Fintype.card_piFinset]
   830	  rw [Fintype.prod_eq_mul_prod_subtype_ne _ j]
   831	  have hsame : Function.update u j s j = s := by simp
   832	  rw [hsame]
   833	  apply congrArg (fun n => s.card * n)
   834	  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
   835	  intro i _
   836	  have hne : Function.update u j s i.1 = u i.1 := by simp [i.2]
   837	  rw [hne]
   838	  simp [u]

   840	/-- The weight of a shared-seed distribution is its fiber cardinality divided
   841	by the cardinality of the seed space. -/
   842	private theorem clDistribution_weight_eq_card_filter_div {K ι : Type*}
   843	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   844	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (z : (ι → K) × (ι → K)) :
   845	    (clDistribution L R).weight z =
   846	      ((Finset.univ.filter fun x => (L x, R x) = z).card : Error) /
   847	        Fintype.card (ι → K) := by
   848	  classical
   849	  rw [clDistribution, Distribution.map_weight, uniformDistribution_support]
   850	  simp [uniformDistribution, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, div_eq_mul_inv,
   851	    mul_comm]
   852	
   853	/-- The CL distribution of coordinate direct sums factors into the component
   854	CL distributions. The equality is stated pointwise on weights, which is the
   855	finite-distribution meaning of the product in `lem:cl-dist-prod`; blueprint
   856	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1141-1146`, paper
   857	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:366-379`. -/
   858	theorem clDistribution_directSum_eq_prod {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   859	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   860	    {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (V : Fin m → Finset ι)
   861	    (ell : Fin m → ℕ)
   862	    (L R : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   863	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   864	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ i, a ∈ V i)
   865	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (L j))
   866	    (hR : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (R j))
   867	    (z : (ι → K) × (ι → K)) :
   868	    (clDistribution (condLinearDirectSum V L) (condLinearDirectSum V R)).weight z =
   869	      ∏ j : Fin m, (clDistribution (L j) (R j)).weight
   870	        (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2) := by
   871	  classical
   872	  let _sourceIndex : Fin m := ⟨0, hm⟩
   873	  let e : (ι → K) ≃ ∀ j, V j → K :=
   874	    coordinatePartitionEquiv V hDisjoint hCover
   875	  let fiber : (j : Fin m) → Finset (V j → K) := fun j =>
   876	    Finset.univ.filter fun x =>
   877	      (L j (extendRegister (V j) x), R j (extendRegister (V j) x)) =
   878	        (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2)
   879	  have hL_support (j : Fin m) (x : ι → K) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) :
   880	      L j x a = 0 :=
   881	    IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem (hL j) x ha
   882	  have hR_support (j : Fin m) (x : ι → K) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) :
   883	      R j x a = 0 :=
   884	    IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem (hR j) x ha
   885	  have hdirect (x : ι → K) :
   886	      (condLinearDirectSum V L x, condLinearDirectSum V R x) = z ↔
   887	        ∀ j,
   888	          (L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x),
   889	              R j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) =
   890	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2) := by
   891	    constructor
   892	    · intro h j
   893	      have hleft : condLinearDirectSum V L x = z.1 := congrArg Prod.fst h
   894	      have hright : condLinearDirectSum V R x = z.2 := congrArg Prod.snd h
   895	      have hleft_parts : ∀ i,
   896	          L i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x) = coordinateRestriction (V i) z.1 := by
   897	        apply (sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover
   898	          (fun i => L i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x))
   899	          (fun i a ha => hL_support i _ a ha) z.1).mp
   900	        exact hleft
   901	      have hright_parts : ∀ i,
   902	          R i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x) = coordinateRestriction (V i) z.2 := by
   903	        apply (sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover
   904	          (fun i => R i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x))
   905	          (fun i a ha => hR_support i _ a ha) z.2).mp
   906	        exact hright
   907	      exact Prod.ext (hleft_parts j) (hright_parts j)
   908	    · intro h
   909	      apply Prod.ext
   910	      · apply (sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover
   911	          (fun i => L i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x))
   912	          (fun i a ha => hL_support i _ a ha) z.1).mpr
   913	        exact fun j => congrArg Prod.fst (h j)
   914	      · apply (sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover
   915	          (fun i => R i (coordinateRestriction (V i) x))
   916	          (fun i a ha => hR_support i _ a ha) z.2).mpr
   917	        exact fun j => congrArg Prod.snd (h j)
   918	  have hglobal_card :
   919	      (Finset.univ.filter fun x =>
   920	          (condLinearDirectSum V L x, condLinearDirectSum V R x) = z).card =
   921	        ∏ j, (fiber j).card := by
   922	    calc
   923	      (Finset.univ.filter fun x =>
   924	          (condLinearDirectSum V L x, condLinearDirectSum V R x) = z).card =
   925	          (Finset.univ.filter fun x : ∀ j, V j → K => ∀ j, x j ∈ fiber j).card := by
   926	            apply card_filter_equiv e
   927	            intro x
   928	            rw [hdirect]
   929	            simp only [fiber, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   930	            constructor
   931	            · intro hx j
   932	              simpa only [e, extendRegister_partition_apply V hDisjoint hCover]
   933	                using hx j
   934	            · intro hx j
   935	              simpa only [e, extendRegister_partition_apply V hDisjoint hCover]
   936	                using hx j
   937	      _ = (Fintype.piFinset fiber).card := by
   938	            congr 1
   939	            ext x
   940	            simp
   941	      _ = ∏ j, (fiber j).card := Fintype.card_piFinset fiber
   942	  have hcomponent_card (j : Fin m) :
   943	      (Finset.univ.filter fun x =>
   944	          (L j x, R j x) =
   945	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2)).card =
   946	        (fiber j).card *
   947	          ∏ i : {i // i ≠ j}, Fintype.card (V i.1 → K) := by
   948	    calc
   949	      (Finset.univ.filter fun x =>
   950	          (L j x, R j x) =
   951	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2)).card =
   952	          (Finset.univ.filter fun x : ∀ i, V i → K => x j ∈ fiber j).card := by
   953	            apply card_filter_equiv e
   954	            intro x
   955	            simp only [fiber, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   956	            rw [extendRegister_partition_apply V hDisjoint hCover]
   957	            rw [IsCondLinearOn.apply_coordinateRestriction (hL j) x]
   958	            rw [IsCondLinearOn.apply_coordinateRestriction (hR j) x]
   959	      _ = (fiber j).card *
   960	          ∏ i : {i // i ≠ j}, Fintype.card (V i.1 → K) :=
   961	        card_filter_pi_apply_mem (fun i => V i → K) j (fiber j)
   962	  have hcard_seed : Fintype.card (ι → K) = ∏ j, Fintype.card (V j → K) := by
   963	    rw [Fintype.card_congr e, Fintype.card_pi]
   964	  have hcomponent_weight (j : Fin m) :
   965	      (clDistribution (L j) (R j)).weight
   966	          (coordinateRestriction (V j) z.1, coordinateRestriction (V j) z.2) =
   967	        ((fiber j).card : Error) / Fintype.card (V j → K) := by
   968	    rw [clDistribution_weight_eq_card_filter_div, hcomponent_card, hcard_seed]
   969	    rw [Fintype.prod_eq_mul_prod_subtype_ne _ j]
   970	    push_cast
   971	    have hcardj : (Fintype.card (V j → K) : Error) ≠ 0 := by positivity
   972	    have hcard_rest :
   973	        (∏ i : {i // i ≠ j}, (Fintype.card (V i.1 → K) : Error)) ≠ 0 := by
   974	      positivity
   975	    field_simp
   976	  rw [clDistribution_weight_eq_card_filter_div, hglobal_card, hcard_seed]
   977	  simp_rw [hcomponent_weight]
   978	  rw [Finset.prod_div_distrib]
   979	  push_cast
   980	  rfl
   981	
   982	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1123-1134`, approached through the

    19	`lem:cl-restriction-idem`, `lem:cl-restriction-sum`,
    20	`lem:cl-supported-restriction`, and `lem:cl-func-prod-same-level` at

    31	/-- A representation of a conditionally linear function supported on a register

    33	auxiliary for `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint `lem:cl-supported-vanishing`. -/
    34	theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    36	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    37	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
    38	    CondLinearTerm.eval t x a = 0 := by
    39	  induction t generalizing S with
    40	  | zero => rfl
    41	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
    42	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
    43	      change (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
    44	        CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x) a = 0
    45	      rw [Pi.add_apply, hSupport _ a (fun haS₁ => ha (hS₁ haS₁))]
    46	      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun haDiff => ha (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp haDiff).1)]
    47	      exact zero_add 0

    49	/-- A supported representation of a conditionally linear function depends only

    60	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩

    63	        by_cases ha : a ∈ S₁

   158	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)) (x : ι → K) :
   159	    CondLinearTerm.eval t x =
   160	      t.headLinear (coordinateRestriction t.headSupport x) +
   161	        CondLinearTerm.eval
   162	          (t.tail (t.headLinear (coordinateRestriction t.headSupport x))) x := by
   163	  cases t
   164	  rfl

   166	/-- The sum of the first linear pieces of a finite family of positive-level
   167	conditionally-linear terms. -/
   168	private def condLinearHeadSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   169	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J] {ell : ℕ}
   170	    (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)) :
   171	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   172	  toFun x := ∑ j, (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (t j).headSupport x)
   173	  map_add' x y := by
   174	    rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   175	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   176	    intro j _
   177	    rw [← map_add]
   178	    congr 1
   179	    ext b
   180	    by_cases hb : b ∈ (t j).headSupport <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, hb]
   181	  map_smul' c x := by
   182	    rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   183	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   184	    intro j _
   185	    rw [← map_smul]
   186	    congr 1
   187	    ext b
   188	    by_cases hb : b ∈ (t j).headSupport <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, hb]
   189	
   190	/-- Combine equal-level representations of conditionally linear functions on
   191	disjoint registers. -/
   192	private def CondLinearTerm.directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   193	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   194	    (V : J → Finset ι) :
   195	    (ell : ℕ) → (J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) →
   196	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   197	  | 0, _ => .zero
   198	  | ell + 1, t =>
   199	      .succ (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) (condLinearHeadSum t)
   200	        (by
   201	          intro x a ha
   202	          simp only [condLinearHeadSum, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk,
   203	            Finset.sum_apply]
   204	          apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   205	          intro j _
   206	          exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   207	            (fun haj => ha (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)))
   208	        (fun y => directSum (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   209	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y)))
   210	
   211	private theorem CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   212	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   213	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   214	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   215	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) :
   216	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t)
   217	      (Finset.univ.biUnion V) := by
   218	  induction ell generalizing V with
   219	  | zero => trivial
   220	  | succ ell ih =>
   221	      have hhead (j : J) : (t j).headSupport ⊆ V j :=
   222	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   223	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   224	      · exact Finset.biUnion_subset.mpr fun j _ =>
   225	          (hhead j).trans (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem V (Finset.mem_univ j))
   226	      · intro y
   227	        have htail (j : J) :
   228	            CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   229	              ((t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) y))
   230	              (V j \ (t j).headSupport) :=
   231	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) _
   232	        have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   233	            Disjoint (V i \ (t i).headSupport) (V j \ (t j).headSupport) := by
   234	          intro i j hij
   235	          exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   236	        have hrec := ih _ hDisjointTail _ htail
   237	        have hunion :
   238	            Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) =
   239	              Finset.univ.biUnion V \
   240	                Finset.univ.biUnion (fun j => (t j).headSupport) := by
   241	          ext a
   242	          constructor
   243	          · intro ha
   244	            obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp ha
   245	            obtain ⟨haV, haS⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hj
   246	            refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr
   247	              ⟨Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haV⟩, ?_⟩
   248	            intro haHeads
   249	            obtain ⟨i, _, hai⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp haHeads
   250	            by_cases hij : i = j
   251	            · subst i
   252	              exact haS hai
   253	            · exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) (hhead i hai) haV
   254	          · intro ha
   255	            obtain ⟨j, _, haV⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).1
   256	            refine Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr
   257	              ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨haV, ?_⟩⟩
   258	            intro haj
   259	            exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp ha).2
   260	              (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩)
   261	        simpa only [hunion] using hrec
   262	
   263	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   264	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   265	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   266	    (ell : ℕ) (t : J → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell)
   267	    (ht : ∀ j, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (t j) (V j)) (x : ι → K) :
   268	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t) x =
   269	      ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   270	  induction ell generalizing V x with
   271	  | zero =>
   272	      apply Eq.symm
   273	      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   274	      intro j _
   275	      cases t j
   276	      rfl
   277	  | succ ell ih =>
   278	      let S : J → Finset ι := fun j => (t j).headSupport
   279	      let y : J → ι → K := fun j =>
   280	        (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   281	      have hS (j : J) : S j ⊆ V j :=
   282	        CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_headSupport (ht j)
   283	      have hy (j : J) (a : ι) (ha : a ∉ V j) : y j a = 0 := by
   284	        exact CondLinearTerm.headLinear_eq_zero_of_not_mem (t j) _
   285	          (fun haS => ha (hS j haS))
   286	      have hhead :
   287	          condLinearHeadSum t
   288	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x) = ∑ j, y j := by
   289	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   290	        intro j _
   291	        change (t j).headLinear
   292	            (coordinateRestriction (S j)
   293	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x)) =
   294	          (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   295	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction
   296	          (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem S (Finset.mem_univ j))]
   297	      have hselect (j : J) : coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i) = y j :=
   298	        coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint y hy j
   299	      have htail (j : J) :
   300	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
   301	        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
   302	      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   303	          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
   304	        intro i j hij
   305	        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   306	      have htail_eval (j : J) :
   307	          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   308	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
   309	            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   310	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   311	        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
   312	          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   313	        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
   314	      have hcomponent (j : J) :
   315	          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
   316	            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   317	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by
   318	        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]
   319	        change (t j).headLinear
   320	              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
   321	            CondLinearTerm.eval
   322	              ((t j).tail
   323	                ((t j).headLinear
   324	                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
   325	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   326	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]
   327	        change y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   328	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   329	        rw [htail_eval]
   330	      have hrec := ih (fun j => V j \ S j) hDisjointTail
   331	        (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) htail x
   332	      have htail_family :
   333	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
   334	            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
   335	        funext j
   336	        rw [hselect]
   337	      calc
   338	        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
   339	            (∑ j, y j) +
   340	              CondLinearTerm.eval
   341	                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
   342	                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by
   343	              change condLinearHeadSum t
   344	                    (coordinateRestriction
   345	                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
   346	                  CondLinearTerm.eval
   347	                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
   348	                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   349	                      (fun j => (t j).tail
   350	                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
   351	                          (condLinearHeadSum t
   352	                            (coordinateRestriction
   353	                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
   354	              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
   355	              rw [htail_family]
   356	        _ = (∑ j, y j) + ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   357	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
   358	        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   359	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
   360	        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   361	              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   362	              intro j _
   363	              exact (hcomponent j).symm
   364	
   365	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   366	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
   367	auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   368	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   369	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   370	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   371	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   372	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   373	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   374	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   375	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   376	  classical
   377	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   378	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   379	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   380	  funext x
   381	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   382	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   383	  intro j _
   384	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   385

    74	/-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/
    75	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.mono_level {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    76	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell k : ℕ}
    77	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)

    81	  rw [← hk]

   105	/-- Prepend one supported linear stage to a family of residual
   106	conditionally-linear maps. -/
   107	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.cons {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   108	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S S₁ : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
   109	    (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   110	    (hS₁ : S₁ ⊆ S) (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
   111	    (R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   112	    (hR : ∀ y, IsCondLinearOn K (S \ S₁) ell (R y)) :

   114	      L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
   115	        R (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)) x) := by

   117	  choose t ht ht_eval using hR
   118	  refine ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport t, ⟨hS₁, ht⟩, ?_⟩

   121	      CondLinearTerm.eval (t (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x = _

   150	private def coordinateRestrictionLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   151	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) :
   152	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   153	  toFun := coordinateRestriction S
   154	  map_add' := coordinateRestriction_add S

   159	private theorem sum_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   160	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   161	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   162	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) :
   163	    ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x = x := by
   164	  classical
   165	  ext a
   166	  obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   167	  rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   168	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, haj]
   169	  · intro i _ hij
   170	    have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   171	      Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   172	    simp [coordinateRestriction, hai]
   173	  · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim

   175	private theorem sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]

275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

   311	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]

   313	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))

   326	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   327	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   328	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}

   331	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :

   344	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]

   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction

   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j

   197	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   198	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   199	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   200	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   201	  toFun x := fun i =>
   202	    match i with
   203	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   204	    | .inl (.inr _) => x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   205	    | .inr _ => 0
   206	  map_add' x y := by
   207	    funext i
   208	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp
   209	  map_smul' c x := by
   210	    funext i
   211	    rcases i with (j | u) | j <;> simp

   213	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map sending the point block to its
   214	canonical line representative in the fixed direction `v` and clearing every
   215	other coordinate. -/
   216	private noncomputable def ldPointCLLinear (P : LdParams) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   217	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   218	  toFun x := fun i =>
   219	    match i with
   220	    | .inl (.inl j) => lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point x) j
   221	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   222	    | .inr _ => 0
   223	  map_add' x y := by
   224	    funext i
   225	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   226	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (x + y)) j = _
   227	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (x + y) = LdSpace.point x + LdSpace.point y := rfl
   228	      rw [hpoint, map_add]
   229	      rfl
   230	    · simp
   231	    · simp
   232	  map_smul' c x := by
   233	    funext i
   234	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
   235	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl
   237	      rw [hpoint, map_smul]
   238	      rfl
   239	    · simp
   240	    · simp

   242	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map zeroing the first `i`
   243	coordinates of the direction block and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   244	private def ldDirectionCLLinear (P : LdParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   245	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   246	  toFun x := fun k =>
   247	    match k with
   248	    | .inl (.inl _) => 0
   249	    | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   250	    | .inr j => prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   251	  map_add' x y := by
   252	    funext k
   253	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   254	    · simp
   255	    · simp
   256	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =
   257	        prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j +
   258	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j
   259	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   260	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]
   261	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   262	        rfl
   263	  map_smul' c x := by
   264	    funext k
   265	    rcases k with (j | u) | j
   266	    · simp
   267	    · simp
   268	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (c • x)) j =
   269	        c • prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction x) j
   270	      by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   271	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, smul_zero]
   272	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]
   273	        rfl

   395	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>

   398	  have hseed :

   400	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   401	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   402	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   403	  have hval :
   404	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   405	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   406	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))

   415	  funext i

   418	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))

    38	private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    39	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    40	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    41	  invFun p := fun i =>

    50	    · cases u
    51	      rfl

    57	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point block of a uniformly random

    59	private theorem map_uniformDistribution_point (L : LdParams) :
    60	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
    61	      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
    62	  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
    63	      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
    64	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
    65	  calc

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.

   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,

   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$

   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}

   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}

   243	\begin{lemma}

    36	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
    37	vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
    38	private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    39	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    40	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    41	  invFun p := fun i =>
    42	    match i with
    43	    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
    44	    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
    45	    | .inr j => p.2 j
    46	  left_inv z := by
    47	    funext i
    48	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
    49	    · rfl
    50	    · cases u
    51	      rfl
    52	    · rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by
    54	    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
    55	    rfl

    57	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point block of a uniformly random
    58	ambient vector is uniform. -/

    60	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
    61	      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
    62	  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
    63	      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
    64	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
    65	  calc
    66	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
    67	        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
    68	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
    69	          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    70	          rfl
    71	    _ = ((uniformDistribution
    72	          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
    73	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
    74	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
    75	          rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]
    76	    _ = uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := uniformDistribution_map_fst

   100	private theorem ldParams_q_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q := by

   105	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the coordinate index of a scalar is
   106	read off from its binary representation. -/
   107	private theorem chiIndex_eq_iff (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) (i : Fin L.m) :
   108	    chiIndex L s = i ↔
   109	      ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val := by
   110	  rw [Fin.ext_iff]
   111	  simp [chiIndex]

   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
   133	  have hstep2 :
   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,
   182	    ← hstep2, hstep3, Nat.card_Ico]
   183	  omega

   323	distribution on the complete type graph. This is `lem:ld-question-typed-cl`,
   324	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, which identifies the sampler with
   325	`def:typed-cl-distributions` (`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1268-1272`); paper
   326	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   327	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (L : LdParams) :
   328	    ldQuestionDistribution L =
   329	      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) (by simp)

   331	  have hgraph : ∀ hE : (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)).Nonempty,
   332	      graphDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) hE =
   333	        uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType) := by
   334	    intro hE
   335	    have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (LdType × LdType)).filter
   336	        fun ab => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)))
   337	        = (Finset.univ : Finset (LdType × LdType)) := by
   338	      simp
   339	    change Distribution.uniformOnFinset _ = _
   340	    rw [hfilter]
   341	    rfl
   342	  have hleft : ldQuestionDistribution L =
   343	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
   344	        (fun uv => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   345	          fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by
   346	    rw [bind_uniformDistribution_map]
   347	    rfl
   348	  have hright : ∀ hE : (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)).Nonempty,
   349	      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) hE (ldCL L) (ldCL L) =
   350	        Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
   351	          (fun uv => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   352	            fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by
   353	    intro hE
   354	    have hfamily : (fun uv : LdType × LdType =>
   355	        (clDistribution (ldCL L uv.1) (ldCL L uv.2)).map
   356	          fun xy => ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))) =
   357	      fun uv : LdType × LdType => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   358	        fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z)) := by
   359	      funext uv
   360	      exact Distribution.map_map _ _ _
   361	    change Distribution.bind (graphDistribution _ hE) _ = _
   362	    rw [hgraph hE, hfamily]
   363	  rw [hleft, hright]

   200	/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
   201	weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
   202	`Distribution`. -/
   203	theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
   204	    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
   205	    μ = ν := by
   206	  cases μ with
   207	  | mk s w hn ho =>
   208	    cases ν with
   209	    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
   210	      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
   211	      have hw : w = w' := hweight
   212	      subst hs
   213	      subst hw
   214	      rfl

   216	/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
   217	Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
   218	theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
   219	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   220	    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
   221	    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
   222	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   223	  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
   224	    rw [Finset.image_image]
   225	    rfl
   226	  · funext c
   227	    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,

   229	      intro a ha
   230	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
   231	      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
   232	    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
   233	    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
   234	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
   235	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a

   238	    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
   239	    congr 1
   240	    ext a
   241	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
   242	    constructor
   243	    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
   244	      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
   245	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩

     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and

     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-520`;
    14	the formalization support nodes `lem:line-rep-kernel` and
    15	`lem:line-rep-incidence` are at `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:522-550`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators
    22	
    23	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    24	
    25	/--
    26	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    27	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`;
    28	paper origin
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    30	-/
    31	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    34	
    35	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    36	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`, paper origin
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    38	-/
    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    41	  Pi.single i 1
    42	
    43	/--
    44	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    45	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    47	-/
    48	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    49	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i

   107	  have hc :
   108	      IsCompl
   109	        (registerSubmodule K
   110	          (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))))
   111	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) :=
   112	    (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement
   113	      (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))).symm
   114	  have hrep : lineRepMap v u =
   115	      (registerSubmodule K
   116	        (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))))).projection
   117	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) hc u := rfl
   118	  rw [hrep, ← Submodule.projection_eq_self_sub_projection hc u]

   180	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :

   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.

   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}
   273	
   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

     6	# Lines, bounded line polynomials, and line-point distributions
     7	
     8	This file provides the seed-bearing line descriptions and coefficient-list
     9	polynomials shared by the observable and combining chapters. It also realizes
    10	the line-point distribution directly from the conditionally linear sampler.
    11	Over a finite coefficient field, bounded individual-degree multivariate
    12	polynomials form a finite outcome set for the associated measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The line and bounded-polynomial definitions are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-86`, with source origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. The
    19	line-point sampler is `def:line-point-dist` in blueprint chapter 13, from
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    21	-/
