   306	/-- The diagonal direction in every sampled description has the prefix-zero
   307	property of `lem:dlnf`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:113-118`, paper
   308	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
   309	theorem dLinePointDist_prefix_zero (L : LdParams) :
   310	    ∀ sample ∈ (dLinePointDist L).support,
   311	      ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L sample.1.seed).val →
   312	        sample.1.direction j = 0 := by
   313	  intro sample hsample
   314	  have hsupport : (dLinePointDist L).support =
   315	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (LdSpace L)).image
   316	        fun z => (ldDLineCL L z, ldPointCL L z)).image
   317	        fun s => (dLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2) := rfl
   318	  rw [hsupport] at hsample
   319	  obtain ⟨s, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hsample
   320	  exact LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero (dLineDescOf L s.1) rfl
   321	
   322	/-- The low-degree question sampler is the typed conditionally linear
   323	distribution on the complete type graph. This is `lem:ld-question-typed-cl`,
   324	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, which identifies the sampler with
   325	`def:typed-cl-distributions` (`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1268-1272`); paper
   326	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
   327	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (L : LdParams) :
   328	    ldQuestionDistribution L =
   329	      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) (by simp)
   330	        (ldCL L) (ldCL L) := by
   331	  have hgraph : ∀ hE : (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)).Nonempty,
   332	      graphDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) hE =
   333	        uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType) := by
   334	    intro hE
   335	    have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (LdType × LdType)).filter
   336	        fun ab => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)))
   337	        = (Finset.univ : Finset (LdType × LdType)) := by
   338	      simp
   339	    change Distribution.uniformOnFinset _ = _
   340	    rw [hfilter]
   341	    rfl
   342	  have hleft : ldQuestionDistribution L =
   343	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
   344	        (fun uv => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   345	          fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by
   346	    rw [bind_uniformDistribution_map]
   347	    rfl
   348	  have hright : ∀ hE : (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)).Nonempty,
   349	      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) hE (ldCL L) (ldCL L) =
   350	        Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (LdType × LdType))
   351	          (fun uv => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   352	            fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z))) := by
   353	    intro hE
   354	    have hfamily : (fun uv : LdType × LdType =>
   355	        (clDistribution (ldCL L uv.1) (ldCL L uv.2)).map
   356	          fun xy => ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))) =
   357	      fun uv : LdType × LdType => (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   358	        fun z => ((uv.1, ldCL L uv.1 z), (uv.2, ldCL L uv.2 z)) := by
   359	      funext uv
   360	      exact Distribution.map_map _ _ _
   361	    change Distribution.bind (graphDistribution _ hE) _ = _
   362	    rw [hgraph hE, hfamily]
   363	  rw [hleft, hright]
   364	
   365	/-- Bounded multivariate polynomials form a finite set over a finite coefficient
   366	semiring. This is the finite outcome set required by `def:ld-meas`,
   367	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:164-171`, paper
   368	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   369	noncomputable instance polyFuncFintype (m : ℕ) (K : Type*)
   370	    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) := by
   371	  letI : Finite ↥(polyFunc m K d) := Module.finite_of_finite K
   372	  exact Fintype.ofFinite _
   373	
   374	/-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite
   375	coefficient semiring. -/
   376	noncomputable abbrev PolyIndex (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   377	    [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)
   378	
   379	/-- A POVM indexed by one bounded multivariate polynomial. -/
   380	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   381	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   382	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] := Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι
   383	
   384	/-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may
   385	have its own coefficient field, number of variables, and degree bound.
   386	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:164-171`, paper
   387	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   388	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
   389	    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
   390	    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   391	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   392	  Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
   393	
   394	/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
   395	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   396	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
   397	
   398	/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   399	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   400	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   401	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
   402	
   403	/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   404	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   405	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   406	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   407	
   408	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   409	point question. -/
   410	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   411	  fun i => match i with
   412	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   413	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   414	  | .inr _ => 0
   415	
   416	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   417	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   418	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   419	
   420	/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
   421	wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
   422	answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   423	def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
   424	  | .pointVals values => values
   425	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   426	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   427	
   428	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   429	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   430	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   431	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   432	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   433	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   434	
   435	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   436	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
   437	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
   438	
   439	The first two consistency bounds compare the point-answer postprocessing of the
   440	strategy with evaluations of the polynomial measurements. Answers of the wrong
   441	form are folded into the zero tuple so that the point family remains a POVM.
   442	
   443	The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
   444	and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
   445	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
   446	`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
   447	theorem exists_ld_soundness :
   448	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   449	      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   450	        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   451	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
   452	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   453	                (fun u outcome =>
   454	                  heteroKron
   455	                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   456	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
   457	                (fun u outcome =>
   458	                  heteroKron 1
   459	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   460	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   461	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   462	                (fun u outcome =>
   463	                  heteroKron
   464	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   465	                (fun u outcome =>
   466	                  heteroKron 1
   467	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   468	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
   469	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   470	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   471	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   472	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   473	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
   474	  sorry
   475	
   476	end

     5	/-!
     6	# Lines, bounded line polynomials, and line-point distributions
     7	
     8	This file provides the seed-bearing line descriptions and coefficient-list
     9	polynomials shared by the observable and combining chapters. It also realizes
    10	the line-point distribution directly from the conditionally linear sampler.
    11	Over a finite coefficient field, bounded individual-degree multivariate
    12	polynomials form a finite outcome set for the associated measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The line and bounded-polynomial definitions are `def:ideg-deg-polynomials` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-86`, with source origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. The
    19	line-point sampler is `def:line-point-dist` in blueprint chapter 13, from
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- A formalization-only identity used to construct canonical line
    33	descriptions: applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has
    34	the same effect as applying it once. -/
    35	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    36	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    37	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    38	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    39	
    40	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    41	inductive LineKind where
    42	  | axis
    43	  | diagonal
    44	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    45	
    46	/-- A seed-bearing line description for `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
    47	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:85-95`, paper
    48	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
    49	
    50	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    51	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    52	Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
    54	corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Multivariate polynomials in `m` variables whose total degree is at most
   110	`d`. This is the class `deg_d` in `def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, blueprint
   111	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:37-48`, paper
   112	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-52`. -/
   113	abbrev TotalDegreePoly (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :=
   114	  {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K // p.totalDegree ≤ d}
   115	
   116	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   117	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   118	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   119	
   120	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   121	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   122	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   123	  fun i =>
   124	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   125	
   126	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   127	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   128	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   129	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   130	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   131	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   132	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   133	
   134	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   135	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   136	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   138	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   139	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   140	  classical
   141	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   142	    some (Classical.choose h)
   143	  else none
   144	
   145	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   147	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   151	
   152	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   153	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   154	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   156	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   157	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   158	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   159	      intro j hj
   160	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   161	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   162	
   163	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   164	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   165	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   166	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   167	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   168	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   169	
   170	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   171	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   172	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   173	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   174	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   175	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   176	
   177	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   178	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   179	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   180	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   181	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   182	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   183	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   184	
   185	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   186	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   187	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   188	  change (aLinePointDist L).totalWeight = 1
   189	  rw [aLinePointDist, Distribution.map_totalWeight, clDistribution,
   190	    Distribution.map_totalWeight]
   191	  exact uniformDistribution_isProbability _
   192	
   193	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   194	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   195	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   196	  change (dLinePointDist L).totalWeight = 1

     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-520`;
    14	the formalization support nodes `lem:line-rep-kernel` and
    15	`lem:line-rep-incidence` are at `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:522-550`.

    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    21	open scoped BigOperators

    23	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]

    25	/--
    26	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    27	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`;
    28	paper origin
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    30	-/
    31	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    34	
    35	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    36	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`, paper origin
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.

    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=

    42	
    43	/--
    44	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    45	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper

    48	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=

    51	/--
    52	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may

    56	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=

    64	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}

    76	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    77	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,

    82	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}

    86	/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the

    88	/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`.  Blueprint

   105	theorem sub_lineRepMap_mem_span {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
   106	    u - lineRepMap v u ∈ Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)) := by
   107	  have hc :
   108	      IsCompl
   109	        (registerSubmodule K
   110	          (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))))
   111	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) :=
   112	    (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement
   113	      (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))).symm
   114	  have hrep : lineRepMap v u =
   115	      (registerSubmodule K
   116	        (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))))).projection
   117	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) hc u := rfl
   118	  rw [hrep, ← Submodule.projection_eq_self_sub_projection hc u]

   122	Formalization support node `lem:line-rep-incidence` for
   123	`def:line-representative` (blueprint

   191	/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions
   192	
   193	The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
   194	elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
   195	distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
   196	game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
   197	linear distributions rely on.

   199	
   200	/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
   201	weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
   202	`Distribution`. -/
   203	theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
   204	    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
   205	    μ = ν := by
   206	  cases μ with
   207	  | mk s w hn ho =>
   208	    cases ν with
   209	    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
   210	      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
   211	      have hw : w = w' := hweight
   212	      subst hs
   213	      subst hw
   214	      rfl
   215	
   216	/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
   217	Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
   218	theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
   219	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   220	    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
   221	    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
   222	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   223	  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
   224	    rw [Finset.image_image]
   225	    rfl
   226	  · funext c
   227	    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
   228	        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
   229	      intro a ha
   230	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
   231	      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
   232	    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
   233	    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
   234	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
   235	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
   236	    rw [← hkey]
   237	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
   238	    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
   239	    congr 1
   240	    ext a
   241	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
   242	    constructor
   243	    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
   244	      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
   245	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
   246	      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩

   248	/-- Every point of a finite type carries the same uniform weight.
   249	Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   250	theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
   251	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
   252	    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
   253	  simp [uniformDistribution]

   255	/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
   256	distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
   257	auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   258	theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
   259	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   260	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
   261	    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
   262	    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
   263	    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
   264	  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
   265	    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
   266	    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
   267	      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
   268	    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
   269	    rwa [hc] at hpos
   270	  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
   271	    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
   272	      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
   273	      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
   274	    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
   275	    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
   276	    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
   277	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   278	  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
   279	    ext b
   280	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
   281	    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
   282	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
   283	      exact hcpos
   284	    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
   285	    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩
   286	  · funext b
   287	    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
   288	      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
   289	    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'
   290	    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b,
   291	        (uniformDistribution α).weight a) = (uniformDistribution β).weight b
   292	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply α a,
   293	      uniformDistribution_weight_apply, Finset.sum_const, hc, nsmul_eq_mul, hcard]
   294	    push_cast
   295	    field_simp

   297	/-- Relabelling along a bijection preserves uniformity.  Formalization-only
   298	auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   299	theorem uniformDistribution_map_equiv {α β : Type*}
   300	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   301	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] (E : α ≃ β) :
   302	    (uniformDistribution α).map E = uniformDistribution β := by
   303	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ 1 fun b => ?_
   304	  have hfilter :
   305	      ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => E a = b) = {E.symm b} := by
   306	    ext a
   307	    simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
   308	  rw [hfilter]
   309	  simp

   312	Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
   313	theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst {α β : Type*}

   316	    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.fst = uniformDistribution α := by

   323	  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]

   329	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

   331	    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.snd = uniformDistribution β := by

   341	/-- Binding a uniform distribution to a family of uniformly seeded
   342	push-forwards is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on the product.
   343	Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.bind`. -/
   344	theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
   345	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   346	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
   347	    (g : α → β → γ) :
   348	    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution α)
   349	        (fun a => (uniformDistribution β).map (g a)) =
   350	      (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map fun p => g p.1 p.2 := by
   351	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   352	  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).biUnion
   353	        (fun a => (Finset.univ : Finset β).image (g a)) =
   354	      (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).image fun p => g p.1 p.2
   355	    ext c
   356	    simp [Prod.exists]
   357	  · funext c
   358	    have hcount :
   359	        ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c).card
   360	          = ∑ a : α, ((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card := by
   361	      simp only [Finset.card_filter]
   362	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   363	    have hinner : ∀ a : α,
   364	        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
   365	          = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
   366	              (1 / (Fintype.card β : Error)) := by
   367	      intro a
   368	      change (∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c,
   369	          (uniformDistribution β).weight b) = _
   370	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply β b,
   371	        Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
   372	    have key : ∀ a : α, (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
   373	        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
   374	        = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
   375	            (1 / ((Fintype.card α : Error) * (Fintype.card β : Error))) := by
   376	      intro a
   377	      rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply, hinner a]
   378	      ring
   379	    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α), (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
   380	        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c) =
   381	      ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c,
   382	        (uniformDistribution (α × β)).weight p
   383	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a, ← Finset.sum_mul,
   384	      Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α × β) p,
   385	      Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hcount, Fintype.card_prod]
   386	    push_cast
   387	    ring

     4	/-! # Typed conditionally linear distributions
     5	
     6	Typed question distributions first sample an ordered edge of the type graph and
     7	then sample the corresponding pair of conditionally linear images of one common
     8	uniform seed.

    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:typed-cl-functions` and `def:typed-cl-distributions` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:601-631`, with paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-94`.

    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT

    21	/-- A typed family whose member at every type is `ell`-level conditionally
    22	linear. This is `def:typed-cl-functions`, blueprint
    23	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:601-606`, paper
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-63`. -/
    25	def IsTypedCondLinearFamily (K T : Type*) [Field K]
    26	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	    (ell : ℕ) (L : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    28	  ∀ t, IsCondLinear ell (L t)
    29	
    30	/-- The typed CL distribution: sample a type pair from the graph distribution,
    31	then bind it to the CL distribution selected by those two types. This is
    32	`def:typed-cl-distributions`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:626-631`, paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    34	noncomputable def typedCLDistribution {K T ι : Type*}
    35	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    36	    [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty)
    38	    (L R : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
    39	    Distribution ((T × (ι → K)) × (T × (ι → K))) :=
    40	  Distribution.bind (graphDistribution E hE) fun uv =>
    41	    (clDistribution (L uv.1) (R uv.2)).map fun xy =>
    42	      ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))

   262	private theorem isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]

   264	    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ 1 (fun x => L x) := by
   265	  refine ⟨.succ Finset.univ L (fun _ i hi => absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi)

   267	  funext x
   268	  have hx : coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) x = x := by
   269	    funext i
   270	    simp [coordinateRestriction]
   271	  show L (coordinateRestriction Finset.univ x) + 0 = L x

   274	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: extend a coefficient vector along an injective
   275	reindexing of registers, setting every coordinate outside the image to zero.
   276	Together with the lemmas that follow it, this supports the transport of
   277	conditional linearity between the register spaces of `def:cl-func`,
   278	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
   279	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/

   281	  Function.extend f u 0

   283	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension recovers the original
   284	coordinates along an injective reindexing. -/
   285	private theorem clExtend_apply {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
   286	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) (k : κ) :
   287	    clExtend f u (f k) = u k :=
   288	  hf.extend_apply u 0 k
   289	
   290	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension vanishes at any coordinate
   291	outside the image of the reindexing. -/
   292	private theorem clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K]
   293	    (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) (i : ι) (h : ∀ k, f k ≠ i) :
   294	    clExtend f u i = 0 :=
   295	  Function.extend_apply' u (0 : ι → K) i
   296	    (fun hex => h hex.choose hex.choose_spec)
   297	
   298	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restriction along an injective reindexing
   299	inverts the extension. -/
   300	private theorem clExtend_comp {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
   301	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) :
   302	    (fun k => clExtend f u (f k)) = u :=
   303	  funext fun k => clExtend_apply hf u k

   305	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension of the zero vector vanishes. -/
   306	private theorem clExtend_zero {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
   307	    (hf : Function.Injective f) : clExtend f (0 : κ → K) = 0 := by
   308	  funext i
   309	  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
   310	  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
   311	    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
   312	  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]

   316	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u v : κ → K) :
   317	    clExtend f (u + v) = clExtend f u + clExtend f v := by
   318	  funext i
   319	  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
   320	  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
   321	    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
   322	  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]

   324	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension commutes with scalars. -/

   326	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (c : K) (u : κ → K) :
   327	    clExtend f (c • u) = c • clExtend f u := by
   328	  funext i
   329	  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
   330	  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
   331	    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
   332	  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]

   334	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a linear map of coefficient vectors
   335	along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports
   336	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
   337	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
   338	private def clReindexLinear {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] {f : κ → ι}
   339	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (L : (κ → K) →ₗ[K] (κ → K)) :
   340	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   341	  toFun x := clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
   342	  map_add' x y := by
   343	    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (x + y) (f k))) =
   344	      clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k))) + clExtend f (L (fun k => y (f k)))
   345	    have h : (fun k => (x + y) (f k)) =
   346	        (fun k => x (f k)) + (fun k => y (f k)) := rfl
   347	    rw [h, map_add, clExtend_add hf]
   348	  map_smul' c x := by
   349	    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (c • x) (f k))) =
   350	      c • clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
   351	    have h : (fun k => (c • x) (f k)) = c • (fun k => x (f k)) := rfl
   352	    rw [h, map_smul, clExtend_smul hf]

   354	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a conditionally linear syntax tree
   355	along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports
   356	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
   357	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
   358	private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
   359	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   360	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   361	  | _, .zero => .zero
   362	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
   363	      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
   364	        (by
   365	          intro x i hi
   366	          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
   367	          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
   368	            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
   369	            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
   370	            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
   371	            exact h _ k hk
   372	          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
   373	            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])
   374	        (fun y => clReindexTerm hf (rest (fun k => y (f k))))

   376	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on
   377	any register containing the image of the original support. -/
   378	private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   379	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   380	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   381	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
   382	      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
   383	      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
   384	  intro ell t
   385	  induction t with
   386	  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
   387	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   388	      intro S T hsupp hST
   389	      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
   390	      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
   391	      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
   392	      intro i hi
   393	      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   394	      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
   395	      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
   396	      intro hmem
   397	      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   398	      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

   400	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: evaluation commutes with the transport of a
   401	conditionally linear syntax tree along an injective reindexing. -/
   402	private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   403	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   404	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   405	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (x : ι → K),
   406	      CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf t) x =
   407	        clExtend f (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   408	  intro ell t
   409	  induction t with
   410	  | zero => intro x; exact (clExtend_zero hf).symm
   411	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   412	      intro x
   413	      have hres : (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k)) =
   414	          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
   415	        funext k
   416	        by_cases hk : k ∈ S₁
   417	        · have hmem : f k ∈ S₁.image f := Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk
   418	          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hmem]
   419	        · have hni : f k ∉ S₁.image f := by
   420	            intro hmem
   421	            obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   422	            exact hk (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')
   423	          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hni]
   424	      have hhead : clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) =
   425	          clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
   426	        show clExtend f (L₁ (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k))) = _
   427	        rw [hres]
   428	      have hcomp : (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
   429	            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
   430	          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   431	        rw [hhead]
   432	        exact clExtend_comp hf _
   433	      show clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) +
   434	          CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf (rest
   435	            (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
   436	              (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)))) x =
   437	        clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) +
   438	          CondLinearTerm.eval
   439	            (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))))
   440	            (fun k => x (f k)))
   441	      rw [hcomp, ih _ x, hhead, ← clExtend_add hf]

   542	        rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm

   606	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and

   608	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   609	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.

   611	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   612	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   613	  let lineEdges :=
   614	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   615	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   616	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   617	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   618	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   619	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   620	  let basisEdges :=
   621	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   622	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   623	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   624	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   625	  let pairEdges :=
   626	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   627	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   628	  let msEdges' :=
   629	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   630	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   631	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   632	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

   720	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   721	  toFun
   722	    | .value a => .inl a
   723	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   724	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   725	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))

   727	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   728	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   729	  invFun
   730	    | .inl a => .value a
   731	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   732	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   733	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   734	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   735	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a

   737	  left_inv := by
   738	    intro x
   739	    cases x <;> rfl
   740	  right_inv := by
   741	    intro x
   742	    cases x with
   743	    | inl a => rfl
   744	    | inr x =>
   745	        cases x with
   746	        | inl a => rfl
   747	        | inr x =>
   748	            cases x with
   749	            | inl a => rfl
   750	            | inr x =>
   751	                cases x with
   752	                | inl a => rfl
   753	                | inr x =>
   754	                    cases x with
   755	                    | inl a => rfl
   756	                    | inr x =>
   757	                        cases x with
   758	                        | inl a => rfl
   759	                        | inr a => rfl

   869	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=

   871	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   872	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   873	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   874	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)

   876	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   877	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   878	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   879	-/
   880	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   881	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   882	  open Classical in
   883	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   884	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   885	      if tA = tB then
   886	        decide (a = b)
   887	      else
   888	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   889	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   890	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   891	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   892	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   893	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   894	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   895	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   896	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   897	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   898	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   899	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   900	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   901	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   902	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   903	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   904	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   905	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   906	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   907	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   908	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   909	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   910	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   911	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   912	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   913	          else true
   914	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   915	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   916	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   917	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   918	          else true
   919	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   920	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   921	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   922	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   923	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   924	    else false

   927	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   928	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   929	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   930	-/
   931	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   932	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   933	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P

   358	private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
   359	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   360	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   361	  | _, .zero => .zero
   362	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
   363	      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
   364	        (by
   365	          intro x i hi
   366	          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
   367	          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
   368	            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
   369	            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
   370	            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
   371	            exact h _ k hk
   372	          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
   373	            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])

   376	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on
   377	any register containing the image of the original support. -/
   378	private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   379	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   380	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   381	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
   382	      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
   383	      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
   384	  intro ell t
   385	  induction t with
   386	  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
   387	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   388	      intro S T hsupp hST
   389	      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
   390	      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
   391	      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
   392	      intro i hi
   393	      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   394	      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
   395	      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
   396	      intro hmem
   397	      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   398	      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

   402	private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   403	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   404	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :

   406	      CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf t) x =
   407	        clExtend f (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   408	  intro ell t
   409	  induction t with
   410	  | zero => intro x; exact (clExtend_zero hf).symm
   411	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   412	      intro x
   413	      have hres : (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k)) =
   414	          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
   415	        funext k

   430	          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by

   439	            (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))))
   440	            (fun k => x (f k)))

940	(this is why we modified the measurements to have only two outcomes).
   941	The key quantity to determine which of these is the case is the following complicated-looking expression:
   942	\begin{equation*}
   943	\gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
   944	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;.
   945	\end{equation*}
   946	If $\gamma = 0$, then these two measurements commute, and if $\gamma = 1$, then these two measurements anticommute
   947	(this fact is established in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness} below).
   948	In the $\gamma = 0$ case, the verifier can check whether these two measurements commute by performing the ``commutation check'',
   949	which asks the provers to simultaneously measure both $\tr(g_{h_X}(u_X) \cdot r_X)$ and $\tr(g_{h_Z}(u_Z) \cdot r_Z)$ and report their values.
   950	In the $\gamma = 1$ case, on the other hand, the measurements anticommute, which implies that they cannot simultaneously be measured.
   951	In spite of this, the verifier can still check that the measurements anticommute by using the Magic Square game from Section~\ref{sec:ms} above.
   952	As was shown in Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, any pair of anticommuting measurements
   953	can be used to form a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game
   954	(and indeed the reverse is true as well: any perfect strategy for the Magic Square game entails a pair of anticommuting measurements).
   955	
   956	Together, these give the main subtests for the game $\game^\pauli$.

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

   760	    [AddCommMonoid K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
   761	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))

   766	    funext a
   767	    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   768	    change (∑ i, extendRegister (V i) (fun b => x b)) a = x a
   769	    rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   770	    · simp [extendRegister, haj]
   771	    · intro i _ hij
   772	      have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   773	        Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj

+private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]

+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :

+      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_

+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :

+          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by

+            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
+          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
+        rw [hhead]

   458	\section{Lines}
   459	
   460	The question distributions of the classical low individual degree game and of
   461	the Pauli basis test (Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}) sample lines in $\F_q^m$;
   462	we record here the definition of lines and their canonical representatives.
   463	
   464	\begin{definition}[Lines]\label{def:line}
   465		A \emph{line} $\ell$ in $\F_q^m$ specified by a pair
   466		$(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$ is the subset
   467		\begin{equation}\label{eq:line-set}
   468			\ell(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m\;.
   469		\end{equation}
   470		The vector $v$ is called a \emph{direction} of $\ell(u,v)$; the case $v = 0$
   471		is explicitly allowed, in which case the line is the singleton $\{u\}$. A
   472		line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate
   473		$i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ for which $v = e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   474		vector of $\F_q^m$; such a line is said to be \emph{parallel to the $i$-th
   475		direction}. A line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists
   476		$i \in \{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ such that $v_1 = v_2 = \dots = v_i = 0$ (for
   477		$i = 0$ the condition is vacuous, so every line is diagonal).
   478	\end{definition}
   479	
   480	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:line-equiv}
   481		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePoints_eq_of_mem}
   482		\leanok
   483		\uses{def:line}
   484		Let $u, v \in \F_q^m$. Then for all $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, we have
   485		$\ell(u,v) = \ell(u',v)$.
   486	\end{proposition}
   487	\begin{proof}
   488		\leanok
   489		\uses{def:line}
   490		Fix $u' \in \ell(u,v)$, so $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$. Any
   491		$a \in \ell(u,v)$ has the form $a = u + sv = u' + (s - t)v$, so
   492		$\ell(u,v) \subseteq \ell(u',v)$. The symmetric argument gives the reverse
   493		inclusion.
   494	\end{proof}
   495	
   496	Thus, for a fixed direction, a line is an equivalence class of its points: the
   497	pair $(u,v)$ representing it can use any base point on the line. A canonical
   498	representation is obtained as follows.

   501		\uses{def:line, def:cl-canonical, prop:line-equiv}
   502		Let $\ell$ be a line in direction $v \neq 0$, and let
   503		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v : \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with
   504		the one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$
   505		(Definition~\ref{def:cl-canonical}). The \emph{canonical representative of
   506		$\ell$} is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   507		\[
   508			u_0 = L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v(u) \qquad \text{for all } u \in \ell\;.
   509		\]
   510		This is well defined: since the image and kernel of $L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ are
   511		complementary, any $u \in \ell$ decomposes uniquely as $u = u_0 + tv$ with
   512		$u_0$ in the image, so $u_0 = u - tv \in \ell$ and

    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}

950	In the $\gamma = 1$ case, on the other hand, the measurements anticommute, which implies that they cannot simultaneously be measured.
   951	In spite of this, the verifier can still check that the measurements anticommute by using the Magic Square game from Section~\ref{sec:ms} above.
   952	As was shown in Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, any pair of anticommuting measurements
   953	can be used to form a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game
   954	(and indeed the reverse is true as well: any perfect strategy for the Magic Square game entails a pair of anticommuting measurements).
   955	
   956	Together, these give the main subtests for the game $\game^\pauli$.
   957	
   958	\begin{definition}[Admissible parameters]\label{def:admissible}
   959	  We say that the tuple $\qldparams=(q, m, d)$ is \emph{admissible} if $q$ is
   960	  an admissible field size (Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $m | q$.
   961	\end{definition}
   962	
   963	
   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show
   966	that it is a (typed) CL distribution.
   967	The question types in the game $\game^\pauli$ are
   968	\begin{equation}
   969	  \label{eq:pauli-type}
   970	  \type^\pauli= \bigl( \{\Point, \ALine, \DLine, \Pauli, \Pair \} \times \{X,Z\} \bigr)
   971	  \cup \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair\}\;,
   972	\end{equation}
   973	where $\type^\ms$ is the question type set of the Magic Square game defined in
   974	Section~\ref{sec:ms}.
   975	
   976	
   977	
   978	
   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1004	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Variable_j$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,9\}$, then set $x_w
  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.
  1009		\end{enumerate}
  1010	\end{enumerate}

  1070	We now specify the corresponding CL functions for each of the question types in
  1071	the Pauli basis test.
  1072	
  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

     3	/-!
     4	# Commuting and anticommuting Pauli tuples
     5	
     6	This module defines the tuple phase used in the Pauli basis test and the
     7	conditional uniform distributions used by its observable analysis.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The definitions and probability bounds formalize `def:anticommuting-tuple`
    12	and `fact:omega-anticomm-prob` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:128-267`, with paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:64-95`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	noncomputable section
    22	
    23	/-- A tuple `(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` over the fixed field model of an admissible
    24	Pauli-test parameter tuple. This is the tuple space of
    25	`def:anticommuting-tuple`, blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:128-148`, paper
    26	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:64-68`. -/
    27	abbrev PauliTuple (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    28	  (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) ×
    29	    (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P
    30	
    31	/-- A Pauli tuple is anticommuting when its phase bit is nonzero. This is
    32	`def:anticommuting-tuple`, blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:128-148`, paper
    33	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:64-68`. -/
    34	def IsAnticommuting {P : AdmissibleParams} (ω : PauliTuple P) : Prop :=
    35	  gammaValue P ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2 ≠ 0
    36	
    37	/-- A Pauli tuple is commuting when its phase bit vanishes. This is the
    38	complementary case in `def:anticommuting-tuple`, blueprint
    39	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:128-148`, paper
    40	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:64-68`. -/
    41	def IsCommuting {P : AdmissibleParams} (ω : PauliTuple P) : Prop :=
    42	  gammaValue P ω.1 ω.2.1 ω.2.2.1 ω.2.2.2 = 0
    43	
    44	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    45	    DecidablePred (@IsAnticommuting P) := Classical.decPred _
    46	
    47	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    48	    DecidablePred (@IsCommuting P) := Classical.decPred _
    49	
    50	/-- The uniform probability of the anticommuting event. This is the first
    51	quantity in `fact:omega-anticomm-prob`, blueprint
    52	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:151-178`, paper
    53	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:70-77`. -/
    54	noncomputable def anticommProb (P : AdmissibleParams) : ℝ :=
    55	  ((Finset.univ.filter (@IsAnticommuting P)).card : ℝ) /
    56	    Fintype.card (PauliTuple P)
    57	
    58	/-- The complementary uniform probability of the commuting event in
    59	`fact:omega-anticomm-prob`, blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:151-178`,
    60	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:70-77`. -/
    61	noncomputable def commProb (P : AdmissibleParams) : ℝ :=
    62	  ((Finset.univ.filter (@IsCommuting P)).card : ℝ) /
    63	    Fintype.card (PauliTuple P)

    71

    86	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an admissible field size is at least two.
    87	Blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:151-178`. -/
    88	private theorem two_le_q (P : AdmissibleParams) : 2 ≤ P.q := by
    89	  obtain ⟨k, hk, hq⟩ := P.hq
    90	  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hk
    91	  rw [hq, hj]
    92	  calc 2 = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
    93	    _ ≤ 2 ^ (2 * j + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
    94	
    95	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an admissible field size is either two or a
    96	multiple of eight, because its binary exponent is odd. Blueprint
    97	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:151-178`. -/
    98	private theorem q_eq_two_or_eight_dvd (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    99	    P.q = 2 ∨ 8 ∣ P.q := by
   100	  obtain ⟨k, hk, hq⟩ := P.hq
   101	  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hk
   102	  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos j with hj0 | hj0
   103	  · left
   104	    rw [hq, hj, hj0]
   105	    norm_num
   106	  · right
   107	    refine ⟨2 ^ (2 * j + 1 - 3), ?_⟩
   108	    rw [hq, hj, show (8 : ℕ) = 2 ^ 3 by norm_num, ← pow_add]
   109	    congr 1
   110	    omega

   112	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: over a commutative ring of characteristic
   113	two, the inner product of two indicator vectors is the product of the
   114	coordinate sums `1 + x_i + z_i`. This is the product expansion used in the
   115	proof of `fact:omega-anticomm-prob`, blueprint
   116	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:196-235`. -/
   117	private theorem sum_indicatorVec_mul_indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K]
   118	    [CharP K 2] {m : ℕ} (x z : Fin m → K) :
   119	    ∑ y : Cube m, indicatorVec x y * indicatorVec z y
   120	      = ∏ i : Fin m, (1 + x i + z i) := by
   121	  have h2 : (2 : K) = 0 := CharTwo.two_eq_zero
   122	  have hev : ∀ (u : Fin m → K) (y : Cube m),
   123	      indicatorVec u y = ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then u i else 1 - u i := by
   124	    intro u y
   125	    simp [indicatorVec, indicatorPoly, apply_ite]
   126	  have hfac : ∀ i : Fin m,
   127	      ∑ b : Bool, ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i))
   128	        = 1 + x i + z i := by
   129	    intro i
   130	    have h1 :
   131	        ∑ b : Bool, ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i))
   132	          = x i * z i + (1 - x i) * (1 - z i) := by
   133	      rw [Fintype.sum_bool]
   134	      simp
   135	    rw [h1]
   136	    linear_combination (x i * z i - x i - z i) * h2
   137	  calc ∑ y : Cube m, indicatorVec x y * indicatorVec z y
   138	      = ∑ y : Cube m, ∏ i : Fin m,
   139	          ((if y i then x i else 1 - x i) * (if y i then z i else 1 - z i)) := by
   140	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   141	        intro y _
   142	        rw [hev x y, hev z y, ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
   143	    _ = ∏ i : Fin m, ∑ b : Bool,
   144	          ((if b then x i else 1 - x i) * (if b then z i else 1 - z i)) := by
   145	        rw [Finset.prod_univ_sum, Fintype.piFinset_univ]
   146	    _ = ∏ i : Fin m, (1 + x i + z i) := Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => hfac i
   147	
   148	/-- The phase bit of a Pauli tuple is the trace of `r_Z r_X` times the product
   149	of the coordinate sums `1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}`. This is the closed form of
   150	`γ(ω)` derived in the proof of `fact:omega-anticomm-prob`, blueprint
   151	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:196-235`. -/
   152	private theorem gammaValue_eq_trace_prod (P : AdmissibleParams)
   153	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) :
   154	    gammaValue P uX uZ rX rZ =
   155	      fixedBinTrace P.model (rZ * (rX * ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i))) := by
   156	  haveI := pauliScalar_charTwo P
   157	  have hprod : (∑ y : Cube P.m, indicatorVec uX y * indicatorVec uZ y)
   158	      = ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i) :=
   159	    sum_indicatorVec_mul_indicatorVec uX uZ
   160	  unfold gammaValue
   161	  congr 1
   162	  rw [← hprod]
   163	  simp only [dotProduct, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
   164	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => by ring
   165	
   166	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the field trace onto the two-element field
   167	takes each of its two values on exactly half of the scalars. This is the final
   168	step of the proof of `fact:omega-anticomm-prob`, blueprint
   169	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:236-249`. -/
   170	private theorem two_mul_card_trace_ne (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   171	    2 * (Finset.univ.filter
   172	        (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a ≠ 0)).card = P.q := by
   173	  classical
   174	  haveI := pauliScalar_charTwo P
   175	  have hK := card_pauliScalar P
   176	  have hadd : ∀ a c : PauliScalar P,
   177	      fixedBinTrace P.model (a + c)
   178	        = fixedBinTrace P.model a + fixedBinTrace P.model c := by
   179	    intro a c
   180	    simp [fixedBinTrace, binTrace]
   181	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ : ∃ b : PauliScalar P, fixedBinTrace P.model b = 1 := by
   182	    have hpos : 0 < P.model.basisDim := by
   183	      obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := P.model.basisDimOdd
   184	      omega
   185	    refine ⟨P.model.basis ⟨0, hpos⟩ * P.model.basis ⟨0, hpos⟩, ?_⟩
   186	    simpa [fixedBinTrace, binTrace] using P.model.selfDual ⟨0, hpos⟩ ⟨0, hpos⟩
   187	  have hbb : b + b = 0 := CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero b
   188	  have himg :
   189	      (Finset.univ.filter
   190	          (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)).image (fun a => a + b)
   191	        = Finset.univ.filter
   192	            (fun a : PauliScalar P => ¬ (fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)) := by
   193	    ext a
   194	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   195	    constructor
   196	    · rintro ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩
   197	      rw [hadd, hc, hb]
   198	      simp
   199	    · intro ha
   200	      refine ⟨a + b, ?_, ?_⟩
   201	      · rw [hadd, hb]
   202	        have hone : fixedBinTrace P.model a = 1 := by
   203	          revert ha
   204	          generalize fixedBinTrace P.model a = t
   205	          revert t
   206	          decide
   207	        rw [hone]
   208	        decide
   209	      · rw [add_assoc, hbb, add_zero]
   210	  have hinj : Function.Injective (fun a : PauliScalar P => a + b) :=
   211	    fun _ _ h => by simpa using h
   212	  have hcard :
   213	      (Finset.univ.filter (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)).card
   214	        = (Finset.univ.filter
   215	            (fun a : PauliScalar P => ¬ (fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0))).card := by
   216	    rw [← himg, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj]
   217	  have hsplit :
   218	      (Finset.univ.filter (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0)).card
   219	          + (Finset.univ.filter
   220	              (fun a : PauliScalar P => ¬ (fixedBinTrace P.model a = 0))).card
   221	        = Fintype.card (PauliScalar P) :=
   222	    Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
   223	  rw [hK] at hsplit
   224	  simp only [ne_eq]
   225	  omega
