   227	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the number of Pauli tuples. Blueprint
   228	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:151-178`. -/
   229	private theorem card_pauliTuple (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   230	    Fintype.card (PauliTuple P) = P.q ^ P.m * (P.q ^ P.m * (P.q * P.q)) := by
   231	  have hK := card_pauliScalar P
   232	  simp [PauliTuple, Fintype.card_prod, hK]
   233	
   234	/-- Twice the number of anticommuting tuples is `q^{m+1}(q-1)^{m+1}`. This is
   235	the exact count established in the proof of `fact:omega-anticomm-prob`,
   236	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:196-249`. -/
   237	private theorem two_mul_card_anticommuting (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   238	    2 * (Finset.univ.filter (@IsAnticommuting P)).card
   239	      = P.q ^ (P.m + 1) * (P.q - 1) ^ (P.m + 1) := by
   240	  classical
   241	  haveI := pauliScalar_charTwo P
   242	  have h2 : (2 : PauliScalar P) = 0 := CharTwo.two_eq_zero
   243	  have hK := card_pauliScalar P
   244	  have htr0 : fixedBinTrace P.model 0 = 0 := by
   245	    simp [fixedBinTrace, binTrace]
   246	  set N := (Finset.univ.filter
   247	    (fun a : PauliScalar P => fixedBinTrace P.model a ≠ 0)).card with hNdef
   248	  have hN : 2 * N = P.q := two_mul_card_trace_ne P
   249	  -- the innermost sum, over the second scalar coordinate
   250	  have hinner : ∀ c : PauliScalar P,
   251	      (∑ r : PauliScalar P, if fixedBinTrace P.model (r * c) ≠ 0 then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
   252	        = if c = 0 then 0 else N := by
   253	    intro c
   254	    by_cases hc : c = 0
   255	    · subst hc
   256	      simp [htr0]
   257	    · rw [if_neg hc, hNdef, Finset.card_filter]
   258	      exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.mulRight₀ c hc)
   259	        (fun r => if fixedBinTrace P.model (r * c) ≠ 0 then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
   260	        (fun a => if fixedBinTrace P.model a ≠ 0 then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
   261	        (fun r => rfl)
   262	  -- the sum over the first scalar coordinate
   263	  have hnzcard :
   264	      (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : PauliScalar P => ¬ (x = 0))).card = P.q - 1 := by
   265	    have h1 : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : PauliScalar P => x ≠ 0))
   266	        = Finset.univ.erase 0 := Finset.filter_ne' _ _
   267	    simp only [ne_eq] at h1
   268	    rw [h1, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ, hK]
   269	  have hmid : ∀ dd : PauliScalar P,
   270	      (∑ rX : PauliScalar P, if rX * dd = 0 then (0 : ℕ) else N)
   271	        = if dd = 0 then 0 else (P.q - 1) * N := by
   272	    intro dd
   273	    by_cases hd : dd = 0
   274	    · subst hd
   275	      simp
   276	    · rw [if_neg hd]
   277	      have hcong : ∀ rX : PauliScalar P,
   278	          (if rX * dd = 0 then (0 : ℕ) else N) = if rX = 0 then 0 else N := by
   279	        intro rX
   280	        by_cases hr : rX = 0
   281	        · simp [hr]
   282	        · rw [if_neg (by simpa using mul_ne_zero hr hd), if_neg hr]
   283	      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hcong x), Finset.sum_ite]
   284	      simp [hnzcard]
   285	  -- the sum over the second point block
   286	  have hDcard : ∀ uX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P,
   287	      (Finset.univ.filter (fun uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>
   288	        ¬ ((∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i)) = 0))).card = (P.q - 1) ^ P.m := by
   289	    intro uX
   290	    have hset : (Finset.univ.filter (fun uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P =>
   291	        ¬ ((∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i)) = 0)))
   292	        = Fintype.piFinset (fun i : Fin P.m => Finset.univ.erase (1 + uX i)) := by
   293	      ext uZ
   294	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Fintype.mem_piFinset,
   295	        Finset.mem_erase, and_true]
   296	      constructor
   297	      · intro h i hi
   298	        refine h ?_
   299	        refine Finset.prod_eq_zero (Finset.mem_univ i) ?_
   300	        rw [hi]
   301	        linear_combination (1 + uX i) * h2
   302	      · intro h hz
   303	        rw [Finset.prod_eq_zero_iff] at hz
   304	        obtain ⟨i, -, hi⟩ := hz
   305	        exact h i (by linear_combination hi - (1 + uX i) * h2)
   306	    rw [hset, Fintype.card_piFinset]
   307	    simp [Finset.card_erase_of_mem, Finset.card_univ, hK]
   308	  have houter : ∀ uX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P,
   309	      (∑ uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P,
   310	          if (∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i)) = 0 then (0 : ℕ) else (P.q - 1) * N)
   311	        = (P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * N) := by
   312	    intro uX
   313	    rw [Finset.sum_ite]
   314	    simp [hDcard uX]
   315	  have step1 : ∀ (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (rX : PauliScalar P),
   316	      (∑ rZ : PauliScalar P,
   317	          if IsAnticommuting ((uX, uZ, rX, rZ) : PauliTuple P) then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
   318	        = if rX * ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i) = 0 then 0 else N := by
   319	    intro uX uZ rX
   320	    have hcongr : ∀ rZ : PauliScalar P,
   321	        (if IsAnticommuting ((uX, uZ, rX, rZ) : PauliTuple P) then (1 : ℕ) else 0)
   322	          = if fixedBinTrace P.model
   323	              (rZ * (rX * ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i))) ≠ 0 then 1 else 0 := by
   324	      intro rZ
   325	      have hiff : IsAnticommuting ((uX, uZ, rX, rZ) : PauliTuple P)
   326	          ↔ fixedBinTrace P.model
   327	              (rZ * (rX * ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i))) ≠ 0 := by
   328	        unfold IsAnticommuting
   329	        rw [gammaValue_eq_trace_prod]
   330	      by_cases h : fixedBinTrace P.model
   331	          (rZ * (rX * ∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i))) ≠ 0
   332	      · rw [if_pos (hiff.mpr h), if_pos h]
   333	      · rw [if_neg (fun hh => h (hiff.mp hh)), if_neg h]
   334	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hcongr x), hinner]
   335	  have hcount : (Finset.univ.filter (@IsAnticommuting P)).card
   336	      = P.q ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * N)) := by
   337	    rw [Finset.card_filter]
   338	    simp only [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   339	    calc (∑ uX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P, ∑ uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P,
   340	            ∑ rX : PauliScalar P, ∑ rZ : PauliScalar P,
   341	              (if IsAnticommuting ((uX, uZ, rX, rZ) : PauliTuple P) then (1 : ℕ) else 0))
   342	        = ∑ _uX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P, (P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * N) := by
   343	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun uX _ => ?_
   344	          rw [← houter uX]
   345	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun uZ _ => ?_
   346	          rw [← hmid (∏ i : Fin P.m, (1 + uX i + uZ i))]
   347	          exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun rX _ => step1 uX uZ rX
   348	      _ = P.q ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * N)) := by
   349	          rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, smul_eq_mul]
   350	          congr 1
   351	          simp [hK]
   352	  rw [hcount]
   353	  have hexpand : 2 * (P.q ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * N)))
   354	      = P.q ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) ^ P.m * ((P.q - 1) * (2 * N))) := by ring
   355	  rw [hexpand, hN, pow_succ, pow_succ]
   356	  ring

   177		A tuple $\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)$ sampled uniformly at random from
   178		$(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$ is anticommuting with probability exactly
   179		\[
   180			\big(1 - q^{-1}\big)^{m+1} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   181		\]

   183		$\frac12$. In particular, if $m \leq q$, then $\omega$ is anticommuting
   184		with probability at least $2^{-4}$ and commuting with probability at
   185		least $\frac12$. If $m, d \geq 1$, then the probability that $\omega$ is
   186		anticommuting is at least
   187		\[
   188			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big(1 - \frac{md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}
   189			\,\geq\, \Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
   190		\]

   192		$\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.

   195		\leanok

   197		By the definition of the indicator vector
   198		(Definition~\ref{def:indicator-vector}), expanding the product over the
   199		coordinates $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ into a sum over $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   200		gives
   201		\[
   202			\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)
   203			\,=\, \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_X)\, \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_Z)
   204			\,=\, \prod_{i=1}^{m} \big( u_{X,i}\, u_{Z,i} + (1 - u_{X,i})(1 - u_{Z,i}) \big)\,,
   205		\]
   206		and since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$, the $i$-th factor equals
   207		$1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$. Hence
   208		\[
   209			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\Big( (r_X r_Z) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}) \Big)\,.
   210		\]
   211		For any fixed $u_X$, the $m$ factors $1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$ are
   212		independent and uniformly distributed in $\F_q$ over the choice of
   213		$u_Z$, so all of them are nonzero with probability $(1-q^{-1})^m$;
   214		independently, $r_X \neq 0$ with probability $1 - q^{-1}$. If $r_X = 0$
   215		or some factor vanishes, then $\gamma(\omega) = 0$. Otherwise, over the
   216		uniform choice of $r_Z$, the argument of the trace is a uniformly random
   217		element of $\F_q$. Since $q = 2^k$ is admissible, the trace of an
   218		element of $\F_q$ equals the coordinate sum of its binary
   219		representation: writing $\kappa$ for the binary representation with
   220		respect to the fixed self-dual normal basis
   221		(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), item~2 of
   222		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   223		$\tr(c) = \tr(c \cdot 1) = \kappa(c) \cdot \kappa(1)$, and $\kappa(1)$
   224		is the all-ones vector by Lemma~\ref{lem:one}. As $\kappa$ is a
   225		bijection onto $\F_2^k$, a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace
   226		$0$ with probability exactly $\frac12$. Combining, the probability that
   227		$\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$ is exactly $(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \cdot \frac12$, and
   228		the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is the complement, which is
   229		at least $\frac12$.
   230	
   231		If $m \leq q$, then
   232		$(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \geq (1-q^{-1})^{q+1} = (1-q^{-1})^{q} \cdot (1-q^{-1})$,
   233		a product of two positive functions of $q$ that are nondecreasing for
   234		$q \geq 2$, so it is minimized at $q = 2$, where it equals $2^{-3}$;
   235		hence the anticommuting probability is at least $2^{-4}$.

   240		the positive factors $1 - q^{-m}$, $1 - q^{-1}$, and $\frac12$ with
   241		the negative factor $1 - md/q$ --- so the anticommuting probability,
   242		being nonnegative, exceeds it. If $md \leq q$, then by Bernoulli's
   243		inequality
   244		$(1-q^{-1})^{m} \geq 1 - m/q \geq 1 - md/q \geq (1-q^{-m})(1-md/q)$,
   245		where the last step multiplies the nonnegative quantity $1 - md/q$
   246		by $1 - q^{-m} \leq 1$; multiplying by $1 - q^{-1}$ shows that the
   247		anticommuting probability is at least the first displayed bound. For
   248		the second inequality of the display, expanding the product shows
   249		that $(1-q^{-m})(1-q^{-1})(1-md/q)$ exceeds
   250		$1 - q^{-m} - q^{-1} - md/q$ by
   251		$q^{-m-1} + \frac{md}{q} \big( q^{-m} + q^{-1} - q^{-m-1} \big)$,

   253		$md \geq 1$ gives $q^{-m} \leq q^{-1} \leq md/q$, the product is

    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}

   338	private def clReindexLinear {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] {f : κ → ι}
   339	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (L : (κ → K) →ₗ[K] (κ → K)) :
   340	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   341	  toFun x := clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
   342	  map_add' x y := by
   343	    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (x + y) (f k))) =
   344	      clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k))) + clExtend f (L (fun k => y (f k)))
   345	    have h : (fun k => (x + y) (f k)) =
   346	        (fun k => x (f k)) + (fun k => y (f k)) := rfl
   347	    rw [h, map_add, clExtend_add hf]

   349	    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (c • x) (f k))) =
   350	      c • clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
   351	    have h : (fun k => (c • x) (f k)) = c • (fun k => x (f k)) := rfl

   358	private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
   359	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   360	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   361	  | _, .zero => .zero
   362	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
   363	      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
   364	        (by
   365	          intro x i hi
   366	          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
   367	          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
   368	            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
   369	            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
   370	            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
   371	            exact h _ k hk
   372	          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
   373	            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])

   376	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on
   377	any register containing the image of the original support. -/
   378	private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   379	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   380	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   381	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
   382	      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
   383	      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
   384	  intro ell t
   385	  induction t with
   386	  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
   387	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   388	      intro S T hsupp hST
   389	      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
   390	      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
   391	      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
   392	      intro i hi
   393	      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   394	      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
   395	      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
   396	      intro hmem
   397	      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   398	      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

   400	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: evaluation commutes with the transport of a
   401	conditionally linear syntax tree along an injective reindexing. -/
   402	private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   403	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   404	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   405	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (x : ι → K),
   406	      CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf t) x =
   407	        clExtend f (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   408	  intro ell t
   409	  induction t with
   410	  | zero => intro x; exact (clExtend_zero hf).symm
   411	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   412	      intro x
   413	      have hres : (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k)) =
   414	          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
   415	        funext k
   416	        by_cases hk : k ∈ S₁
   417	        · have hmem : f k ∈ S₁.image f := Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk
   418	          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hmem]
   419	        · have hni : f k ∉ S₁.image f := by
   420	            intro hmem
   421	            obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   422	            exact hk (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')
   423	          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hni]
   424	      have hhead : clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) =
   425	          clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
   426	        show clExtend f (L₁ (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k))) = _
   427	        rw [hres]
   428	      have hcomp : (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
   429	            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
   430	          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   431	        rw [hhead]
   432	        exact clExtend_comp hf _
   433	      show clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) +
   434	          CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf (rest
   435	            (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
   436	              (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)))) x =
   437	        clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) +
   438	          CondLinearTerm.eval
   439	            (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))))
   440	            (fun k => x (f k)))
   441	      rw [hcomp, ih _ x, hhead, ← clExtend_add hf]

   793	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=

   797	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true

   809	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)

   811	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   812	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   813	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,

   844	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=

   855	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=

   857	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   858	      (a * (match W with
   859	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z

   871	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   872	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   873	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   874	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)

   880	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   881	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   882	  open Classical in
   883	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   884	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   885	      if tA = tB then
   886	        decide (a = b)
   887	      else
   888	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   889	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   890	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   891	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   892	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   893	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   894	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   895	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   896	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   897	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   898	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   899	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   900	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   901	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   902	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   903	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   904	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   905	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   906	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   907	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   908	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   909	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   910	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   911	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   912	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   913	          else true
   914	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   915	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   916	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   917	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   918	          else true
   919	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   920	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   921	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   922	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   923	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   924	    else false

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   126	Every point lies on the line through its own canonical representative in the
   127	same direction; this is the incidence property used by the line-versus-point
   128	samplers.

   130	theorem mem_linePoints_lineRepMap {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :

   132	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v u)
   133	  exact ⟨t, by rw [ht]; abel⟩

    36	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
    37	vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
    38	private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
    39	    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
    40	  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
    41	  invFun p := fun i =>
    42	    match i with
    43	    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
    44	    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
    45	    | .inr j => p.2 j
    46	  left_inv z := by
    47	    funext i
    48	    rcases i with (j | u) | j
    49	    · rfl
    50	    · cases u
    51	      rfl
    52	    · rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by
    54	    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
    55	    rfl

    64	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)

    67	        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
    68	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
    69	          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    70	          rfl
    71	    _ = ((uniformDistribution
    72	          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
    73	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
    74	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
    75	          rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]

   100	private theorem ldParams_q_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q := by
   101	  obtain ⟨j, -, hj⟩ := L.hq
   102	  rw [hj]

   105	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the coordinate index of a scalar is
   106	read off from its binary representation. -/
   107	private theorem chiIndex_eq_iff (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) (i : Fin L.m) :
   108	    chiIndex L s = i ↔
   109	      ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val := by
   110	  rw [Fin.ext_iff]
   111	  simp [chiIndex]

   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
   133	  have hstep2 :
   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,
   182	    ← hstep2, hstep3, Nat.card_Ico]
   183	  omega

   380	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]

   384	/-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may
   385	have its own coefficient field, number of variables, and degree bound.
   386	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:164-171`, paper
   387	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   388	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
   389	    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
   390	    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   391	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   392	  Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
   393	
   394	/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
   395	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   396	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
   397	
   398	/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   399	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   400	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   401	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
   402	
   403	/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   404	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   405	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   406	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   407	
   408	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   409	point question. -/
   410	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   411	  fun i => match i with
   412	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   413	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   414	  | .inr _ => 0
   415	
   416	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   417	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   418	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   419	
   420	/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
   421	wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
   422	answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   423	def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
   424	  | .pointVals values => values
   425	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   426	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   427	
   428	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   429	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   430	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   431	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   432	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   433	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   434	
   435	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   436	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
   437	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
   438	
   439	The first two consistency bounds compare the point-answer postprocessing of the
   440	strategy with evaluations of the polynomial measurements. Answers of the wrong
   441	form are folded into the zero tuple so that the point family remains a POVM.
   442	
   443	The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
   444	and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
   445	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
   446	`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
   447	theorem exists_ld_soundness :
   448	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   449	      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   450	        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   451	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
   452	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   453	                (fun u outcome =>
   454	                  heteroKron
   455	                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   456	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
   457	                (fun u outcome =>
   458	                  heteroKron 1
   459	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   460	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   461	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   462	                (fun u outcome =>
   463	                  heteroKron
   464	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   465	                (fun u outcome =>
   466	                  heteroKron 1
   467	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   468	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
   469	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   470	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   471	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   472	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   473	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
   474	  sorry
   475	
   476	end
   477	
   478	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}
   273	
   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space, and their conditional-linearity levels are
    12	established below; the line-point distributions they induce are analysed in
    13	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    32	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    33	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    34	`def:ld-game` in
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, with paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    37	-/
    38	structure LdParams where
    39	  q : ℕ
    40	  m : ℕ
    41	  d : ℕ
    42	  k : ℕ
    43	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    44	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    45	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    46	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    47	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    48	
    49	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    50	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    51	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    52	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    53	
    54	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    55	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    56	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    60	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    61	
    62	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    63	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    64	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    65	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    66	-/
    67	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    68	
    69	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    72	-/
    73	inductive LdType where
    74	  | point
    75	  | aline
    76	  | dline
    77	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    78	
    79	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    82	-/
    83	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    84	
    85	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    88	-/
    89	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    90	
    91	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   101	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   102	
   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   105	-/
   106	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   107	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   108	
   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   177	
   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   180	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   181	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   182	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   183	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   184	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   185	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}
   186	
   187	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   188	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   189	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   190	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j) : LdIndex P)
   191	
   192	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the direction
   193	coordinates of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   194	private def ldDirectionRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   195	  Finset.univ.image fun j : Fin P.m => (Sum.inr j : LdIndex P)
   196	
   197	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the linear map retaining the shared scalar
   198	coordinate and clearing every other coordinate. -/
   199	private def ldSeedLinear (P : LdParams) :
   200	    LdSpace P →ₗ[ScalarQ P] LdSpace P where
   201	  toFun x := fun i =>

+/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions
+
+The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
+elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
+distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
+game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
+linear distributions rely on.
+-/
+
+/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
+weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
+`Distribution`. -/
+theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
+    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
+    μ = ν := by
+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl
+
+/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
+theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
+    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
+    rw [Finset.image_image]
+    rfl
+  · funext c
+    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
+        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
+      intro a ha
+      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
+      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
+    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
+    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
+        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
+      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
+    rw [← hkey]
+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
+    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
+    congr 1
+    ext a
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
+      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
+      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩

+/-- Every point of a finite type carries the same uniform weight.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
+  simp [uniformDistribution]

+/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
+distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
+    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
+    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
+  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
+    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
+    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
+      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
+    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
+    rwa [hc] at hpos
+  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
+    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
+      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))

+    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
+    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
+    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
+    ext b
+    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
+    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
+      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
+      exact hcpos
+    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
+    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩
+  · funext b
+    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
+      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
+    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'

+/-- Relabelling along a bijection preserves uniformity.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_equiv {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] (E : α ≃ β) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map E = uniformDistribution β := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ 1 fun b => ?_
+  have hfilter :
+      ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => E a = b) = {E.symm b} := by
+    ext a
+    simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
+  rw [hfilter]
+  simp

+/-- The first marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.fst = uniformDistribution α := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card β) fun a => ?_
+  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.1 = a)

+      Finset.mem_singleton, and_true]

+  simp

+/-- The second marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/

+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :

+/-- Binding a uniform distribution to a family of uniformly seeded

+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.bind`. -/
+theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (g : α → β → γ) :
+    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution α)
+        (fun a => (uniformDistribution β).map (g a)) =
+      (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map fun p => g p.1 p.2 := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).biUnion
+        (fun a => (Finset.univ : Finset β).image (g a)) =
+      (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).image fun p => g p.1 p.2

+    simp [Prod.exists]
+  · funext c
+    have hcount :
+        ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c).card
+          = ∑ a : α, ((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card := by
+      simp only [Finset.card_filter]
+      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    have hinner : ∀ a : α,
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
+          = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
+              (1 / (Fintype.card β : Error)) := by
+      intro a
+      change (∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c,
+          (uniformDistribution β).weight b) = _
+      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply β b,
+        Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
+    have key : ∀ a : α, (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
+        = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
+            (1 / ((Fintype.card α : Error) * (Fintype.card β : Error))) := by
+      intro a
+      rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply, hinner a]
+      ring

+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c) =

+      Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α × β) p,
+      Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hcount, Fintype.card_prod]

+    ring

   203	theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
   204	    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
   205	    μ = ν := by
   206	  cases μ with
   207	  | mk s w hn ho =>
   208	    cases ν with
   209	    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
   210	      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
   211	      have hw : w = w' := hweight
   212	      subst hs
   213	      subst hw
   214	      rfl

   222	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_

   255	/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform

   258	theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
   259	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
   260	    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
   261	    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
   262	    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
   263	    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
   264	  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
   265	    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
   266	    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
   267	      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
   268	    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
   269	    rwa [hc] at hpos
   270	  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
   271	    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
   272	      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
   273	      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
   274	    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
   275	    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
   276	    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
   277	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   278	  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
   279	    ext b
   280	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
   281	    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
   282	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
   283	      exact hcpos
   284	    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
   285	    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩

   287	    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by

   289	    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'

   292	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply α a,

     4	# Canonical Pauli basis test parameters
     5	
     6	This file defines the canonical admissible parameter tuple as a function of

     8

    10	
    11	The definitions and estimate correspond to `def:introparams` and
    12	`lem:delta-bound` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:471-492`, from
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1503-1562`.
    15	-/

    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	/-- The admissibility predicate for a parameter tuple `(q, m, d)`. -/
    22	def IsAdmissibleTuple (t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) : Prop :=
    23	  IsAdmissibleSize t.1 ∧ 1 ≤ t.2.1 ∧ 1 ≤ t.2.2 ∧ t.2.1 ∣ t.1
    24	
    25	/-- Convert an admissible tuple to the parameter structure used by the
    26	Pauli basis game. -/
    27	def AdmissibleParams.ofTuple (t : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)
    28	    (h : IsAdmissibleTuple t) : AdmissibleParams where
    29	  q := t.1
    30	  m := t.2.1
    31	  d := t.2.2
    32	  hd := h.2.2.1
    33	  hq := h.1
    34	  hdvd := h.2.2.2
    35	
    36	/-- The smallest even natural number represented by the ceiling prescription
    37	in `def:introparams`. -/
    38	noncomputable def introParamsC (a b : ℝ) : ℕ :=
    39	  2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊
    40	
    41	/-- The canonical `(q, m, d)` tuple of `def:introparams`. -/
    42	def introParamsTuple (c R : ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ :=
    43	  (2 ^ (c * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1),
    44	    2 ^ Nat.log 2 (c * Nat.clog 2 R + 1), 1)
    45	
    46	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a numerical comparison of the two exponents
    47	appearing in the canonical tuple.  If `s` is positive and `r` is at most
    48	`2 ^ s`, then the base-two logarithm of `c * r + 1` does not exceed
    49	`c * s + 1`. -/
    50	private theorem log_two_le_mul_add_one (c r s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    51	    (hrs : r ≤ 2 ^ s) : Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ c * s + 1 := by
    52	  have hkey : c * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (c * s + 1) := by
    53	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with hc | hc
    54	    · subst hc
    55	      simp
    56	    · obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, c = d + 1 := ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩
    57	      have h1 : d + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
    58	      have h2 : (d + 1) * r ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := Nat.mul_le_mul h1 hrs
    59	      have h3 : 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    60	        have hp : 0 < 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by positivity
    61	        omega
    62	      have h4 : 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) = 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    63	        rw [pow_add, pow_succ]
    64	        ring
    65	      have h5 : d + 1 + s ≤ (d + 1) * s + 1 := by
    66	        have hds : d ≤ d * s := by
    67	          simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul (le_refl d) hs
    68	        have hexp : (d + 1) * s = d * s + s := by ring
    69	        omega
    70	      calc (d + 1) * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s :=
    71	            Nat.add_le_add h2 h3
    72	        _ = 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) := h4.symm
    73	        _ ≤ 2 ^ ((d + 1) * s + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) h5
    74	  calc Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 (2 ^ (c * s + 1)) :=
    75	        Nat.log_mono_right hkey
    76	    _ = c * s + 1 := Nat.log_pow (by norm_num) _
    77	
    78	/-- The canonical tuple is admissible. This is the numerical
    79	admissibility part of `lem:delta-bound`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:484-492`, paper
    81	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`. -/
    82	theorem introParamsTuple_isAdmissible (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
    83	    IsAdmissibleTuple (introParamsTuple (introParamsC a b) R) := by
    84	  have hEven : Even (introParamsC a b) := ⟨⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊, two_mul _⟩
    85	  have hpow : Nat.clog 2 (2 ^ 2) ≤ Nat.clog 2 R :=
    86	    Nat.clog_mono_right 2 (by simpa using hR)
    87	  have hr2 : 2 ≤ Nat.clog 2 R := by
    88	    rwa [Nat.clog_pow 2 2 (by norm_num)] at hpow
    89	  have hs1 : 1 ≤ Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) := Nat.clog_pos (by norm_num) hr2
    90	  have hrs : Nat.clog 2 R ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) :=
    91	    Nat.le_pow_clog (by norm_num) _
    92	  exact ⟨⟨introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 (Nat.clog 2 R) + 1,
    93	      (hEven.mul_right _).add_one, rfl⟩,
    94	    Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by norm_num), le_rfl,
    95	    pow_dvd_pow 2 (log_two_le_mul_add_one _ _ _ hs1 hrs)⟩
    96	
    97	/-- The canonical admissible parameter structure of `def:introparams`,
    98	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:471-482`, paper
    99	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1503-1514`. -/
   100	noncomputable def introParams (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
   101	    AdmissibleParams :=
   102	  AdmissibleParams.ofTuple _ (introParamsTuple_isAdmissible a b R hR)
   103	
   104	/-- The canonical parameter dimension supplies at least `R` encoded
   105	coordinates, as asserted in `lem:delta-bound`. -/
   106	theorem le_two_pow_introParams_m (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b)
   107	    (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
   108	    R ≤ 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := by
   109	  have hc2 : 2 ≤ introParamsC a b := by
   110	    have hceil : 0 < ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊ :=
   111	      Nat.ceil_pos.mpr (div_pos (by linarith) (by linarith))
   112	    show 2 ≤ 2 * ⌈(b + a) / (2 * b)⌉₊
   113	    omega
   114	  have hlt : introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1 <
   115	      2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1) * 2 := by
   116	    simpa [pow_succ] using
   117	      Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (b := 2) (by norm_num)
   118	        (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1)
   119	  have hmul : 2 * Nat.clog 2 R ≤ introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R :=
   120	    Nat.mul_le_mul hc2 (le_refl _)
   121	  have key : Nat.clog 2 R ≤
   122	      2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1) := by
   123	    omega
   124	  calc R ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 R := Nat.le_pow_clog (by norm_num) R
   125	    _ ≤ 2 ^ (2 ^ Nat.log 2 (introParamsC a b * Nat.clog 2 R + 1)) :=
   126	        Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) key
   127	    _ = 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := rfl

   129	/-- `lem:delta-bound`: the Pauli soundness error at the canonical parameters

   131	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:484-492`, paper

  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a numerical comparison of the two exponents
+appearing in the canonical tuple.  If `s` is positive and `r` is at most
+`2 ^ s`, then the base-two logarithm of `c * r + 1` does not exceed
+`c * s + 1`. -/
+private theorem log_two_le_mul_add_one (c r s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
+    (hrs : r ≤ 2 ^ s) : Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ c * s + 1 := by
+  have hkey : c * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (c * s + 1) := by
+    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with hc | hc
+    · subst hc
+      simp
+    · obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, c = d + 1 := ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩
+      have h1 : d + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
+      have h2 : (d + 1) * r ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := Nat.mul_le_mul h1 hrs
+      have h3 : 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by

+private theorem isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (L : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K)) :
+    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ 1 (fun x => L x) := by

+    funext i

+blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
+private def clExtend {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) : ι → K :=
+  Function.extend f u 0

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension recovers the original
+coordinates along an injective reindexing. -/

+    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) (k : κ) :
+    clExtend f u (f k) = u k :=
+  hf.extend_apply u 0 k

+    (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) (i : ι) (h : ∀ k, f k ≠ i) :
+    clExtend f u i = 0 :=
+  Function.extend_apply' u (0 : ι → K) i
+    (fun hex => h hex.choose hex.choose_spec)

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restriction along an injective reindexing

+    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) :
+    (fun k => clExtend f u (f k)) = u :=
+  funext fun k => clExtend_apply hf u k

+  funext i

+  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h

+  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]

+  by_cases h : ∃ k, f k = i
+  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := h
+    simp [clExtend_apply hf]
+  · simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ h]

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a linear map of coefficient vectors
+along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports
+`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
+private def clReindexLinear {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) (L : (κ → K) →ₗ[K] (κ → K)) :
+    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
+  toFun x := clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
+  map_add' x y := by
+    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (x + y) (f k))) =
+      clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k))) + clExtend f (L (fun k => y (f k)))
+    have h : (fun k => (x + y) (f k)) =
+        (fun k => x (f k)) + (fun k => y (f k)) := rfl
+    rw [h, map_add, clExtend_add hf]
+  map_smul' c x := by
+    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (c • x) (f k))) =
+      c • clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
+    have h : (fun k => (c • x) (f k)) = c • (fun k => x (f k)) := rfl
+    rw [h, map_smul, clExtend_smul hf]
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a conditionally linear syntax tree
+along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports
+`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
+private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
+  | _, .zero => .zero
+  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
+      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
+        (by
+          intro x i hi
+          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
+          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
+            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
+            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
+            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
+            exact h _ k hk
+          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
+            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])
+        (fun y => clReindexTerm hf (rest (fun k => y (f k))))

+any register containing the image of the original support. -/
+private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
+      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
+      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
+  intro ell t
+  induction t with
+  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
+      intro S T hsupp hST
+      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp

+      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
